traceability.notes:
Story 022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE is fully implemented.
The core parser behavior requested by the story has been added in the valid-annotation-format rule via normalizeCommentLine and isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine, and is wired into processCommentLine so that: - Traceability annotations (@story, @req, @supports) are parsed as before, with multi-line support. - Any subsequent non-traceability JSDoc tag line (e.g. @param, @returns) cleanly terminates the current annotation value (REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION, REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION, REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC). - Continuations occur only on lines that do not begin with another JSDoc tag, preserving multi-line paths/IDs while preventing JSDoc tags from being concatenated (REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE). - The specific bug cited in the story (REQ-OPTIMIZATION followed by @param) is covered by an explicit positive test ensuring no error is reported (REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES).
Comprehensive tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts cover all tag positions (before, after, mixed), multi-line values, and the exact previously failing scenario. These tests are explicitly annotated as supporting this story and its requirement IDs, and they all pass in the current Jest run. Documentation in docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md has been updated with a dedicated "JSDoc coexistence" section that both describes the behavior and provides concrete examples including Story 022.0.
Given the passing tests, explicit story/requirement traceability, updated implementation, and updated documentation, all acceptance criteria for this story are satisfied.
